entries.clue: Covers loosely with cropped top and trousers (8)

indicatorNotes.cropped: a cropped word has its end cut off, as hair is cropped short

blocks.note: top = BEST, as in 'the best'; cropped loses its last letter
trews are close-fitting tartan trousers

annotation.surface: Someone throws a skimpy top and some trousers loosely over a chair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as a garment beside the trousers, but it is the adjective meaning finest.
annotation.definitionFit: Scattering things over a surface covers it loosely, the old sense of strewing.

entries.clue: Live around flightless birds in muddle (6)

indicatorNotes.around: BE is placed around the birds, enclosing them

blocks.note: to be = to live, exist
emus cannot fly

annotation.surface: A picture of living among flightless birds in some disorder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Muddle' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to confuse or bewilder someone is to muddle them.

entries.clue: Nicks from old swords caught (6)

indicatorNotes.caught: what is caught by the ear is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: steel is an old poetic word for a sword; the plural, heard, is spelt as another word

annotation.surface: Someone pilfers antique swords and is caught red-handed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the thief's arrest, but it means heard. Steel for sword is poetic usage, hence 'old'.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: to nick something is to pilfer it.

entries.clue: Scoundrel and lunatic brought up in N Sea port (9)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, bringing a word up writes it from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rotter is a cad or scoundrel
lunatic = MAD, written upwards

annotation.surface: A villain and a madman are hauled into a North Sea harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: Rotter is dated British slang for a scoundrel.
annotation.definitionFit: The great Dutch harbour on the North Sea, Europe's biggest port.

entries.clue: Alcoholic drinks, assuredly not some 1917 reds (5,8)

blocks.note: a cocktail of vodka, coffee liqueur and cream
the side that fought the Red Bolsheviks after the 1917 revolution

annotation.surface: A drinks list that pointedly rules out anything from the Russian Revolution's red side.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition works by opposition: the Russians who were certainly not Reds in 1917 were the Whites.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is a vodka, coffee liqueur and cream cocktail; the other is the anti-Bolshevik side of the Russian Civil War.

entries.clue: Printed – and hightailed it (3,3)

blocks.note: copies are printed by running them through a press
to hightail it is to flee in a hurry

annotation.surface: Someone prints something and then bolts.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are everyday phrasal verbs; the dash only separates them.
annotation.definitionFit: Copies are printed by running them off a press, and to hightail it is to flee.

entries.clue: Old soldier and mother heading up to see friend in Seville (5)

indicatorNotes.heading up: in a down clue, heading up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: O = old, a standard abbreviation
a GI is an American soldier
ma = mother

annotation.surface: A veteran and his mother head north to visit a friend in Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old soldier' looks like one unit, a veteran, but splits into O and GI; the whole string is then written upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a friend, as a Sevillian would say it.

entries.clue: Took place in company, rising, better – about right? (8)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, a rising word is written upwards
indicatorNotes.about: the word for better goes about R, surrounding it

blocks.note: Co. = company, written upwards
to cure is to make better
R = right, placed inside the previous piece

annotation.surface: Something happened in a business on the rise that was doing better, apparently properly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb, to make well, not the adjective the surface uses; 'about right?' reads as a hesitant aside but places the R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an event that happened has taken place.

entries.clue: Tricky; finished struggling (8)

indicatorNotes.struggling: letters that struggle thrash about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A solver's verdict on a hard puzzle: tricky, and still battling to finish.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a solver's complaint about this very sort of puzzle, which hides that 'finished' is simply the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Devilishly hard, as a puzzle can be, is a stronger sense of tricky.

entries.clue: Musical aces exhibiting supreme talent regarding instrumentation, primarily? (7)

annotation.definition: Musical aces exhibiting supreme talent regarding instrumentation, primarily?

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily points to the prime, first letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Musical aces exhibiting supreme talent regarding instrumentation
blocks.note: first letters of the seven words

annotation.surface: Praise for virtuosos whose mastery shows above all in how they handle instruments.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of star musicians, which is why the first letters start at the very first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plural of the Italian for master, used for great conductors and virtuosos, whose supreme talent the whole clue describes.

entries.clue: Round child tucked in to cheese roll (7)

indicatorNotes.tucked in to: the pieces are tucked inside the cheese

blocks.note: O is round in shape
ch. = child, a standard abbreviation
brie is a soft French cheese; the other pieces go between BRI and E

annotation.surface: A child tucks into a round of cheese on a roll.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tucked in to' reads as eating, but it means placed inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A sweet, buttery French bread roll enriched with egg.

entries.clue: Pleased by ‘cake’ that’s reconstituted pulses (5-4,4)

indicatorNotes.reconstituted: reconstituted means built up again, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is delighted to be served 'cake' that is really rehydrated beans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reconstituted' is the natural word for soaking dried pulses, which keeps it hidden as an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Dried beans with a dark spot, a staple pulse of the American South.

entries.clue: Decipher crossword’s clues? Only about five (5)

indicatorNotes.about: the word for only goes about the five, surrounding it

blocks.note: sole = only
V is the Roman numeral five

annotation.surface: A solver sighs that only about five clues have been cracked.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a progress report on this very puzzle; the question mark marks the definition as playful rather than a dictionary one.
annotation.definitionFit: Working out a puzzle's answers is what deciphering its clues amounts to.

entries.clue: Attracted by quirky demeanour (9)

indicatorNotes.quirky: quirky means odd, so the letters are oddly arranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is drawn to another person's odd manner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attracted by' reads as one phrase, but 'by' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: Being charmed and drawn to someone, usually followed by 'of' or 'with'.

entries.clue: Ken sends urn toppling in debauchery (11)

indicatorNotes.toppling: letters that topple fall into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A reveller called Ken knocks an urn over during a wild night.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints the answer itself: a reveller knocking things over.
annotation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking is one of the classic forms of debauchery.

entries.clue: Less well behaved; more like Fanny Adams? (9)

blocks.note: the comparative of a word for mischievous
sweet Fanny Adams means nothing, so this asks for a made-up comparative of a word for zero; the question mark flags it

annotation.surface: Asking whether someone is becoming as badly behaved as a person called Fanny Adams.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweet Fanny Adams, or sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all, so something more like it is more like naught.
annotation.definitionFit: Worse behaved in the ordinary sense; in the cryptic sense, closer to nought, which sweet Fanny Adams means.

entries.clue: Performed with a cold jerk that’s preachy (8)

blocks.note: to do a play is to perform it
as printed
C = cold, as on taps
a tic is an involuntary jerk

annotation.surface: An actor with a cold and a twitch gives a moralising performance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a person, but it is a twitch.
annotation.definitionFit: Tending to instruct and moralise, which is what preachy people do.

entries.clue: On LSD, that’s staggering (8)

blocks.note: high on a hallucinogen, having an acid experience
stumbling, catching one's feet

annotation.surface: Someone high on acid is reeling about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' could be the adjective meaning amazing, but here it is stumbling.
annotation.definitionFit: A hallucinogenic high is a trip, and stumbling over one's feet is the other sense.

entries.clue: Everyman has room for improvement, reader: honestly! (1,7,3)

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I
someone with potential has room to improve and grow; 'has' just attaches it
the reader of the clue is addressed as you

annotation.surface: The setter owns up to the reader that he could do better, honestly.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's name standing for I, and the reader for YOU, are clue-writing conventions.
annotation.definitionFit: An emphatic assurance of sincerity, used just as 'honestly!' is.

entries.clue: President’s computer working to suppress resistance (6)

indicatorNotes.to suppress: to suppress is to hold something in, so the computer and working hold R inside

blocks.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
R = resistance, the physics symbol
on = working, switched on

annotation.surface: The French President's laptop is used to crush opposition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' reads as political opposition; in wordplay it is the symbol R from electrics. The ’s is short for 'is' and links.
annotation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron, President of France since 2017.

entries.clue: Avoid dunce’s cap, excelling (though only somewhat) (6)

indicatorNotes.though only somewhat: only some of the words are used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'dunce's' through 'cap' into the start of 'excelling'

annotation.surface: A pupil escapes the dunce's cap by doing well, though only moderately.
annotation.walkthrough: The parenthesis reads as a tongue-in-cheek aside about the pupil, which is how the hidden-word signal hides.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to get away from something is to avoid it.

entries.clue: Central character in Dungeons & Dragons? (9)

blocks.note: the surface means the hero of a story; the setter means a typed symbol sitting in the middle
the surface means the fantasy game; the setter means its printed title, whose middle symbol is &

annotation.surface: Asks who the main hero is in the fantasy role-playing game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a hero of the game but is really a typographic character, and the one in the middle of the title is &.
annotation.definitionFit: The symbol & is a typographic character, and it stands in the middle of the game's title.

entries.clue: Governor that’s needed by draughtsman (5)

blocks.note: a governor is one who holds power over a state
a draughtsman needs a straight-edge marked in measurements

annotation.surface: A governor whom a technical draughtsman cannot do without.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a description rather than a synonym: the thing a draughtsman needs.
annotation.definitionFit: One who governs, and the straight-edge a draughtsman draws lines with.

entries.clue: Manages nuts and loaves (5)

blocks.note: to lead a team is to manage it
nut is slang for the top of the body
loaf is slang for the same thing, as in 'use your loaf'

annotation.surface: A list of what a bakery or shop deals in: nuts and loaves.
annotation.walkthrough: This is really three definitions. 'Use your loaf' is British rhyming slang, loaf of bread for head.
annotation.definitionFit: To lead is to manage; nut and loaf are both slang for the thing on your shoulders.

entries.clue: Desserts with flirts (7)

blocks.note: layered British puddings of sponge, fruit, custard and cream
a verb: toys with someone's affections

annotation.surface: Puddings served with a side of flirtation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flirts' is a verb here, not the plural noun the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: Layered sponge-and-custard puddings, and a verb for toying with someone's affections.

entries.clue: Land – ground – earthier – not hard (7)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground up, so the letters are broken and rearranged
indicatorNotes.not: 'not hard' asks for EARTHIER without the letter H, since hard is H on pencil grades

blocks.note: EARTHIER without H, hard, as on pencils
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A list about soil: land, ground, something earthier but softer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Land' and 'ground' look like a pair of synonyms, but only 'Land' defines; 'ground' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A country on the Red Sea coast in the Horn of Africa.

entries.clue: Vacantly idling in vehicles: they’ll produce smoke (6)

indicatorNotes.Vacantly: a word emptied of its middle leaves only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one piece inside another, as someone sits in a vehicle

blocks.note: IDLING emptied leaves I and G
cars are vehicles; the other piece goes between C and ARS

annotation.surface: Cars sitting with engines idling pump out exhaust.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the smoke come from the idling engines; the definition points elsewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: Rolled tobacco leaves, lit and puffed, give off smoke.

entries.clue: Some priest ran Georgia, leading to disunite (8)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the word is used, a piece of it

blocks.note: the tail end of 'priest'
as printed
GE is the country code for Georgia

annotation.surface: A priest who ran the country of Georgia split it apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ran' is used as printed, and Georgia is the country, whose code is GE.
annotation.definitionFit: To alienate people from each other is to disunite them.
